values.c0442.t0: proposed ownership entity (name pending) is raising €2.5 million to take control of PAS Giannina FC, the only professional football club in Epirus, northwestern Greece, and return it to the Greek Super League. The club spent 13 of the 15 seasons before 2024-25 in the top flight. An ownership collapse, not a sporting one, then took it down two divisions in two seasons and wound up the old operating company. The club's name, history, stadium, and supporters are intact. The balance sheet that sank it is not coming with us.
values.c0443.t0: We are entering through a new company. No shares in the old entity change hands. Investors receive 80% of the ownership group, the managing partner holds 20% and runs the club full time from Ioannina, and the amateur association keeps the 10% Greek law reserves for it, with no role in operations. The capital funds entry, the legacy government debt on 20-year terms, two full seasons of operations, and a contingency reserve.
values.c0444.t0: The plan is one promotion per season: out of the third tier this year, out of Super League 2 next, then a second round at a higher valuation to build a squad that stays in the top flight. Comparable Greek Super League clubs have traded between €10 million and €15 million. OFI Crete, a regional club with a profile like ours, just won the Greek Cup and qualified for the Europa League. The path from a club like this to European football exists, and it has been walked in the last twelve months.
values.c0445.t0: We will not close unless the numbers hold. Sponsorship letters of intent will be signed before the transaction closes. The conservative model must show a solvent club. And if the litigation between the club's previous operators touches the new entity in any way, we do not proceed.
values.c0447.t0: Greece is the lowest-cost entry into a top-flight European league with a real path to UEFA competition. In England, Italy, or Spain, buying a first-division club and keeping it there costs tens or hundreds of millions. In Greece, a well-run club can reach the Super League, and from there the Europa League or Conference League, on a budget that wouldn't cover one Premier League player's salary.
values.c0448.t0: Three things make this market attractive right now:
values.c0449.t0: The football is getting better. Greece has finished in the top 10 of UEFA's country coefficient ranking in each of the last two seasons. Greek clubs have eliminated sides from Italy, England, and France in European competition, and in 2024 a Greek club won a major European trophy for the first time in history.
values.c0450.t0: The country-coefficient claim in the source brief requires a current-season refresh.
values.c0451.t0: Smaller Greek clubs are already proving it. OFI Crete, a regional club outside the big four, won the Greek Cup in 2026 and qualified for the Europa League. The proof of concept exists: a well-run club from outside Athens and Thessaloniki can reach Europe and collect the money that comes with it.
values.c0452.t0: The clubs are still run like it's 1995. Outside the top four or five, most Greek clubs have no structured scouting, no analytics in decision-making, underfunded academies, and commercial operations that stop at the stadium gates. The bar is low. Clearing it is a competitive advantage.
values.c0453.t0: What would be marginal gains in a big-five league is transformational in Greece. That is the whole thesis.
values.c0455.t0: PAS Giannina FC is the club of Ioannina, capital of the Epirus region. The city has roughly 110,000 residents; the wider region is home to more than 330,000. There is no competing professional sports team anywhere in the region. The territory belongs to the club alone.
values.c0456.t0: A Super League club by history
values.c0457.t0: Before 2024-25, PAS Giannina had spent 13 of the previous 15 seasons in the Greek Super League, competing against the country's biggest sides, reaching a Greek Cup semi-final, and qualifying for the early rounds of European competition. The club has a long record of putting young players in front of bigger clubs and moving them on for fees, including transfers to Arsenal and VfB Stuttgart.
values.c0458.t0: What happened, and why it is the opportunity
values.c0459.t0: The decline was an ownership story from start to finish. After the death of the club's long-time owner, his family took over and the club was relegated within a season. Two unstable years followed, with a change of operator, unpaid obligations, and a second relegation. In 2026 the old operating company was placed into liquidation and the club's amateur association, its supporters and former players, took charge of the football section with a stated goal: hand a functioning team to a serious investor.
values.c0460.t0: That is what makes the entry clean. There are no shares in a failed company to buy and no seller to negotiate with. A new entity takes on the club with its name, crest, history, stadium, and fan base, on terms set with the supporters who kept it alive. This is a reset, not a rescue.
values.c0462.t0: A passionate, loyal fan base with a regional identity no other club can claim
values.c0463.t0: An uncontested territorial footprint across all of Epirus
values.c0464.t0: A platform to showcase young players in a top-flight environment and move them on for profit, with a track record of doing exactly that
values.c0465.t0: A population and geography that can support a scalable youth academy
values.c0466.t0: A clean corporate slate: a new entity, a known and manageable legacy debt, and no ownership dispute attached
values.c0468.t0: Epirus punches above its size as a brand. Ioannina is a lakeside university city beneath the Pindus Mountains. On the coast, Parga and Syvota draw visitors from across Europe every summer. Inland, Zagori and the Vikos Gorge sit inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. Urban, coastal, alpine: it is a commercial and cultural story that most Greek clubs simply don't have to tell.
values.c0470.t0: The club currently plays in Gamma Ethniki, Greece's third tier. The route to the Super League is two promotions, and we plan to take them in consecutive seasons.
values.c0478.t0: A professional operation in an amateur league. Low wage bill, best-in-division staff, analytics-led recruitment of free agents. This is the cheapest season the club will ever have.
values.c0482.t0: A 16-team professional league where the top two go up. Full licensing, the operating model in this brief, sponsorship and streaming revenue online.
values.c0486.t0: A second capital round at a higher valuation, invested directly into the first-team squad so the club stays up and builds toward UEFA qualification.
values.c0487.t0: If a promotion slips a season, the plan does not break. The club is solvent, professionally run, free of the failures that took it down, and positioned for a better-funded push the following year. The goal is long-term sustainability, not short-term speculation.
values.c0489.t0: The football operation is the backbone of this project. Nothing else works without it. We plan to set the benchmark for modern club operations in Greece, from the pitch to the balance sheet. Four pillars:
values.c0490.t0: Football decisions built on data. Analytics inform every recruitment, selection, and coaching decision. In Greece's lower divisions clubs do not pay transfer fees, so the market is free agents and undervalued players, and the club that identifies them best wins. A global scouting network spanning Europe, South America, and Mexico, and an advisory bench that has negotiated transfers with AC Milan, Arsenal, Dortmund, and West Ham, give us that edge from day one.
values.c0491.t0: Player development as a business line. An academy that develops the region's youth, and a first team that gives young players a top-flight stage and moves them on for profit. Develop, sell, reinvest. This becomes a core revenue engine once the club is back in the Super League, and the margins from it compound every advantage we have. A dedicated sports science department covers recovery, nutrition, injury prevention, and conditioning from the first team down to the academy.
values.c0492.t0: A 21st-century commercial operation. No club in Greece is doing real commercial numbers globally. Commercial revenue stops at the stadium gates and the regional sponsor. We will build the club as a global brand from day one: creative kit and merchandise strategies, digital-first partnerships, content distribution, and on-the-ground activations in the diaspora markets where Greek football already has an audience nobody is selling to.
values.c0493.t0: Financial discipline. Sponsorship letters of intent secured before close. Two full seasons of runway plus a contingency reserve so the club is never undercapitalized. A second raise on promotion, at a higher valuation, rather than stretching this round.
values.c0495.t0: Neither the Super League nor Super League 2 has an international TV deal. Millions of Greeks and Greek-descended fans in the United States, Australia, and Germany have no way to watch a regional club. We will stream our matches to them ourselves, possibly free to start, to get people through the door and build the audience, then monetize it through sponsors who want to reach that market. The cost is minimal. The upside is a direct relationship with a global fan base, and a position in front of the American market that no Greek club currently occupies. Beyond the match feed, we intend to build a streaming culture around the club: influencers at games, their audiences interacting live, the club as content. It is exploratory by design, and it is the most asymmetric bet in this plan: very low cost, very high reward.

values.c0595.t0: €3.125 million is a small number in European football. For context:
values.c0596.t0: AEK Athens (Super League) was purchased in 2024 for €90 million.
values.c0597.t0: OFI Crete (Super League), a regional club comparable in size and support to PAS Giannina, was available in January 2022 for €15 million. In 2026 it won the Greek Cup and qualified for the Europa League.
values.c0598.t0: On promotion to the Super League, we believe PAS Giannina FC is worth €15 million using traditional Greek football valuation models, before any of our modernization strategies are applied. At that mark, the investor group's 80% of the ownership group is worth roughly €10.8 million, over four times the capital in this round. With structured football operations, a data-driven front office, and a real commercial engine, we expect to separate from those peer clubs, not match them.

values.c0601.t0: Promotion is the trigger for the next raise. At a higher valuation, with the club in the Super League and the operating model proven, we raise again and invest directly in first-team talent to fortify the squad for the top flight. Investors in this round hold the position that round is priced against. From there the objectives are a properly built academy, the premier football operation in the region, and the qualifying rounds of UEFA competition within three seasons of promotion.
values.c0603.t0: A Conference League campaign brings in around €5 million. A Europa League campaign brings in around €15 million, between league-phase fees, performance bonuses, broadcasting allocations, and UEFA coefficient payments. In a league where most clubs operate on under €7 million a year, one European campaign puts PAS Giannina in a financial tier above the majority of its domestic competition. And it is not theoretical: OFI Crete, a regional club with a comparable profile, is in the Europa League right now after winning the 2026 Greek Cup. The exposure does the rest: brand visibility, market credibility, and sponsorship demand that a lower-division club cannot generate.

values.c0605.t0: RISKS, AND HOW WE HANDLE THEM
values.c0606.t0: Two promotions, not one. Neither is guaranteed. The model funds two full seasons regardless of results, and a missed promotion leaves a solvent, debt-light club rather than a crisis.

values.c0609.t0: Greek football governance. Licensing, federation process, and regional politics are real friction for outsiders. We are not outsiders. Our team is Greek, connected from the federation to regional government, and has spent its careers inside the system.
values.c0610.t0: Key person. The managing partner is relocating to Ioannina and this is his sole focus. He is supported by a football operations lead, a strategic advisor with deep Epirus roots, and directors of scouting and sports science.
values.c0612.t0: Conti Kolokotronis, Managing Partner and Chief Executive
values.c0613.t0: Conti Kolokotronis combines elite football development, professional playing experience, and commercial expertise. As a youth player he trained in the academies of AC Milan, FC Barcelona, River Plate, and PAOK Thessaloniki, playing alongside future World Cup winners across three continents, before a professional career in Greece that ended through injury. He then moved into sports marketing and branding, working with Fly Nowhere and collaborating with Manchester United, the Sacramento Kings, and the Athletics. He sourced and negotiated this transaction, is relocating to Ioannina to run the club full time, and will lead both the football operation and the commercial vision.
values.c0615.t0: A product of the AEK Athens academy and a former professional in Greece, Lampros Lampropoulos brings deep institutional knowledge of Greek football. Fluent in Greek and English and connected across the domestic landscape, he bridges the club to agents, coaches, and local talent pipelines and supports every football-side activity, from scouting and staff recruitment to player negotiations and development strategy.
values.c0617.t0: Kostas Farras is a Greek-German football agent, born in Germany with family roots in Epirus, with a global network built over decades in the sport. He has negotiated deals with AC Milan, Arsenal, Werder Bremen, Borussia Dortmund, VfB Stuttgart, and West Ham United, and has personally facilitated transfers from PAS Giannina to Arsenal and Stuttgart. His deals include two of the ten largest transfers ever involving Greek internationals: Sokratis Papastathopoulos (€16 million to Arsenal, 2018) and Konstantinos Mavropanos (€20 million to West Ham, 2023).
values.c0618.t0: Maximiliano Roditis, Director of Global Scouting
values.c0619.t0: A former professional in Argentina, Greece, and Mexico, Maximiliano Roditis oversees international scouting. Based between California, Greece, and Argentina, with strong ties in Mexico, he brings on-the-ground insight from the regions that consistently produce undervalued talent and will shape the club's global recruitment strategy.
values.c0620.t0: Fotis Stefanis, Director of Sports Science
values.c0621.t0: A two-time Olympian who represented Cyprus in the pole vault at the 1992 and 2000 Games, Fotis Stefanis has trained multiple Olympians over the past decade. Based in Athens, he will build the sports science department from the first team to the academy.
values.c0623.t0: Greek football remains overlooked, undervalued, and underbuilt. PAS Giannina FC is a rare combination of regional loyalty, proven top-flight history, and scalable potential, available on a clean slate at the lowest entry point in its modern history. The club has the foundation to play in Europe. The window to take it there is open right now, and it will close the moment the club is back in the professional leagues and priced like one.

values.runtime.years.2.title: Stay. Establish. Then look toward Europe.
